messages.author: 75b7e35a905299c5
messages.subject: Obtaining p-values for LDSC
parts:
Hi,

How do you obtain the p-value for the genetic correlation using the function ldsc? I notice that the output is the rg and the corresponding se, but I am not sure how to obtain the corresponding p-value.

Thank you for your help!

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining p-values for LDSC
parts: the ratio of the estimate to its standard error can be used to determine the p value using the pnorm function in R, taking care about whether you are interested in a 1 or 2 tailed p value..

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining p-values for LDSC
parts:
the most straightforward way is to specify a model in genomic sem that represents a saturated covariance matrix and then look at the standardized output and associated SEs.
Michel's Rpub actually shows this as an example: https://rpubs.com/MichelNivard/640145
as with below "the ratio of the estimate to its standard error can be used to determine the p value using the pnorm function in R, taking care about whether you are interested in a 1 or 2 tailed p value..."
elliot
